Modern Foreign Languages
“Learning another language is not only learning different words for the same things but learning another way to think about things.” Flora Lewis
At Headcorn School we believe that the learning of a modern foreign language provides a valuable educational, social and cultural experience for our pupils. They develop linguistic competence, extend their knowledge of how language works and explore the differences and similarities between the foreign language (French, in our case) and English. Learning another language raises awareness of our multilingual and multicultural world and gives them an insight into their own culture and that of others. It also provides a medium for cross-curricular links and for reinforcement of the knowledge, skills and understanding developed in other subjects.
In KS2 we follow Language Angles, which enables children to progress in all aspects of language learning: oracy, literacy, intercultural understanding, and knowledge about language. We use a variety of techniques to encourage children to engage actively in their learning. These include rhymes, songs, games, using repetition and actions to help learn new vocabulary, and role-play. We emphasise listening, responding, and speaking skills along with simple reading and writing activities, aiming to make the learning of a new language as fun and enjoyable as possible.

Music
“Music can change the world” Beethoven
Our Vision for Music at Headcorn Primary School...
At Headcorn, Music is at the heart of our school. It is incorporated across the curriculum with other subjects, including MFL, where the children learn to sing French songs. Music lessons are taught in correlation with the Charanga music scheme, once a week across the school, in which our pupils develop their skills in listening, appraising, performing and composing. The children in Key Stage 1 and Reception develop knowledge of the musical elements of pulse, rhythm, pitch and tempo. This progresses in Key Stage 2 to exploring dynamics, timbre, texture, structure and notation, using the knowledge of these elements to inspire and compose pieces of music by the end of Year 6.
Each term, the children learn to perform a song from the scheme in order to enrich their performance skills, through singing and the playing of instruments. Our pupils explore a variety of instruments throughout their school lives, including voice in Reception, handbells in Year 1, ocarina in Year 2, recorder in Year 3, ukulele in Year 4, guitar in Year 5 and voice in Year 6. The children are also given many opportunities to learn instruments in formal lessons with music professionals who teach during school time. Furthermore, our pupils are encouraged to share their musical talents with their classmates by performing to each other in assemblies and during class music sessions. The children at Headcorn leave the school with an appreciation for music borne of exposure to a wide variety of music styles and cultures and, it is intended, a lifelong enjoyment of the subject.

pageCache.text:
Attendance and Absences
At Headcorn Primary School, good attendance is essential for children to achieve their best. When children attend regularly, they make better progress, build friendships and feel part of the school community.
We aim for excellent attendance for every pupil and encourage 100% attendance wherever possible.
If a child’s attendance falls below 96%, we may contact parents to offer support and work together to improve attendance.
Children should arrive by 8.50am each day.
All late arrivals must report to the school office with a parent or carer.
Reporting an Absence
If your child is absent, please contact the school on the first day of absence before 9.00am.
This is important so we know that every child is safe.
Telephone: 01622 891289 Email: admin@headcorn.kent.sch.uk
Absence due to illness will usually be authorised.
If your child is absent for more than 5 days, the school may ask for medical evidence, such as an appointment card, prescription or doctor’s note.
Medical Appointments
Please try to arrange appointments outside of school hours where possible.
If this is not possible, inform the school in advance and ensure your child is absent for the shortest time necessary.
Term-time leave is rarely authorised.
Leave may only be granted by the Headteacher in exceptional circumstances, such as:
Family holidays during term time will not normally be authorised.
Unauthorised absence may result in a penalty notice issued by the local authority.
Supporting Good Attendance
If your child is finding it difficult to attend school, please contact us as soon as possible. We will work with you to understand any barriers and provide support.
Together, we can help every child attend regularly and make the most of their learning.

Governors
School Governors
The Governing Body is a group of 10 individuals, made up of parents, staff and members of the local community. We work on a voluntary basis to support the strategic leadership of the school. Governors typically serve for four years, and will have a variety of responsibilities during this time. Whilst the Governing Body carries many legal responsibilities for the school, this only represents part of the overall story. These activities include:
In addition to these, Governors are visible within the school and play an active part in celebrating the success of the children.
Our Vision for Headcorn Primary School
We are proud and passionate about our school and it shows. At Headcorn we offer a safe, nurturing and inclusive environment which encourages every child to understand and respect themselves and others. We are innovative and every day we create opportunities for learning and growth in a happy and vibrant community.
We deliver a strong, varied and exciting curriculum which challenges every child to reach their individual potential. We make effective use of our unique school resources to facilitate learning within and outside the classroom.
We continually enhance our children’s physical and social development and build resilience in an ever-changing world.
We listen and adapt to the shared voice of children, staff and parents. We aspire to excellence for our school community. We embrace opportunities for our children and our staff.
The school and our pupils are active members of the wider community, eager to participate with enthusiasm within the village. Our children are excited about their future roles and responsibilities in their global society.

If you would like to find out more about the general work of the Governors, please feel free to contact me via the school office or by email to the School Business Manager, Mrs Henderson: naomi.henderson@headcorn.kent.sch.uk
Contacting the Governors...
The Governors are always available and happy to receive comments or questions relating to their work and responsibilities at any time. However, depending on your enquiry, it is worth checking first who is best placed to help you.
Day-to-day administrative queries regarding the school should be addressed to the school office. Teaching or classroom queries should be directed to teaching staff, and any queries regarding special educational needs should be directed to our Inclusion Leader. Any further questions or comments relating to the day-to-day running of the school should be directed to the Head Teacher. However, anyone with any comments, queries or questions regarding the overall strategic running of the school, and how the school’s performance is monitored, should contact the Governors.
Many of the Governors are at or around the school on a daily basis, and you are welcome, time permitting, to have an informal word with them at any time. More official communication should be put in writing to the Chair of Governors, Mr T. Kelly, and can be dropped off by hand at the school office, or posted to the school at the normal postal address.
